_README: CANDIDATE RESEARCH — Vietnam for American travelers. All template sections are retained. Verified means the stated claim was supported by an opened official source; it does not mean publication approval. Null or empty values represent unresolved research, not negative findings. Evidence metadata is recorded as strings in _open_questions.value to preserve the template's exact field structure. Recommendations are editorial judgments, not independently verified rankings. All serve_live values remain null.

locale.money_framing: express costs in USD with Vietnamese dong (VND) equivalents

_fact_field_shape: FACTS retain the supplied {value, source_url, status, notes where provided} structure. Evidence entries in _open_questions.value supply source_kind, checked_at, review_after, scope and precise support for the named records. Dates use Europe/Paris. Review dates are editorial research deadlines, not legal expiration dates. No unsupported fact is populated through model confidence.

visa._note: Scope: ordinary, full-validity U.S. passports, tourism, applicants outside Vietnam, and entry through an authorized checkpoint. Special exemptions, emergency passports, employment and residence require separate verification. The maximum visa duration does not guarantee that every applicant receives that duration.

by_nationality.passport: United States ordinary passport; tourism; no separately established exemption

type.notes: E-visa eligibility extends to citizens of all countries under Resolution 127/NQ-CP, effective 2023-08-15. This is a visa category, not a visa waiver. U.S. State Department guidance separately confirms that American tourists generally need a visa before travel.

processing_time.value: Usually 3–5 working days after complete application and payment; not guaranteed.

online_authorization_required.notes: An e-visa is distinct from an arrival declaration. State Department guidance says non-Vietnamese passport holders arriving by air must submit a declaration within three days before arrival. https://prearrival.immigration.gov.vn/ opened without substantive instructions. Independent confirmation of implementation and exceptions remains unresolved; a blanket authorization boolean would be misleading.

notes.value: State Department guidance conflicts internally: one blank page per stamp versus two blank pages. It says e-visas cannot be extended domestically. Immigration separately describes possible sponsored new visas; that is not an e-visa extension. Sources: https://travel.state.gov/en/international-travel/travel-advisories/vietnam.html and https://evisa.xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn/trang-chu-ttdt. Special passport and exemption cases remain unresolved.

approx_rate_note.notes: No current USD/VND conversion was retrieved. Do not reuse the tourism page's historical conversion examples.

cash_vs_card.value: Carry dong for street vendors and small purchases. Many hotels, restaurants and tour businesses accept international cards; acceptance is not universal.

atm_availability.value: ATMs accepting international cards are available at major airports and in cities. Arrange cash before visiting remote destinations.

currency_import_export_limit.value: Declare cash exceeding USD 5,000 equivalent in foreign currency or VND 15,000,000 on entry or exit; these are declaration thresholds.

tipping_norm.value: No fixed national tipping rule. Restaurant and cafe tips are generally optional; tipping is more common for private guides and spa services.

Rental availability must not be presented as permission to drive.

climate_by_season.value: Hanoi: cool or cold and misty December–March; hot, humid and rainy June–August. Hue: wetter September–February. Hoi An: wetter September–January. Ho Chi Minh City and Mekong Delta: rainy May–November, generally drier December–April. These are seasonal patterns, not forecasts.

Alternatives: autumn for a northern focus; December–April for a southern focus. Heat tolerance and exact destinations can change the choice.

safety_health._note: Official advisory and medical recommendations are dated evidence, not guarantees of safety or individualized medical advice. Review before publication and again before travel.

main_risk.value: Petty theft; unexploded ordnance in affected areas.

vaccines.value: CDC recommends keeping routine vaccinations current, hepatitis A for eligible unvaccinated travelers and hepatitis B for unvaccinated travelers of all ages. Japanese encephalitis vaccination depends on duration, rural exposure and activities. Malaria prevention is itinerary-specific: CDC lists no transmission in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Hai Phong, Nha Trang or Quy Nhon, but identifies rural risk areas. Arrange a travel-health assessment at least a month before departure when possible. These are health recommendations, not visa requirements.

dress_norms.value: Dress modestly at religious sites. Cover shoulders and knees; remove hats when entering temples or pagodas. Keep swimwear to beaches and resorts.

UNRESOLVED — E-visa fees and complete application workflow: evisa.gov.vn, its /faq and /instruction pages, and thithucdientu.gov.vn could not be substantively opened. Search snippets are not accepted as verification. The legacy FAQ redirected to login. Fee remains null; current photo specifications, form fields, payment charges and correction procedures require direct confirmation.

UNRESOLVED — Arrival declaration: implementing date, checkpoint coverage, transit exceptions, submission requirements and enforcement were not independently confirmed from readable Vietnamese immigration instructions. Do not equate the declaration with an ETA, an e-visa or optional consular registration.

UNRESOLVED — Immigration exceptions: Phu Quoc-only entry and transit conditions, overseas-Vietnamese exemption documentation, dual nationality, emergency passports, onward tickets and sponsored replacement-visa eligibility require case-specific verification.

SOURCE DIFFERENCE — https://vietnam.travel/faqs still describes 30-day e-visas for 46 countries. The immigration portal and embassy material support the later 90-day framework and all-country eligibility. The FAQ's old eligibility and duration statements were rejected.

SOURCE DIFFERENCE — https://vietnam.travel/plan-your-trip/official-vietnam-evisa-application retains an older application link and a checkpoint list associated with the 2023 framework. Do not treat that list as exhaustive for travel in 2026 or later; confirm the intended land, river, sea or air checkpoint directly with immigration.

SOURCE DIFFERENCE — The Da Nang destination page recommends some September–October travel, while the broader climate guide warns of autumn storm and flooding exposure in nearby central destinations. Different destination scopes and editorial simplification prevent a blanket central-Vietnam weather conclusion.

SOURCE LIMITATION — The tourism transport page gives differing end-to-end train-duration descriptions. No precise rail duration or timetable was adopted. Operator schedules and station-to-station routing are required before itinerary publication.
